title: Kadane's decision
prompt: In `running = Math.max(nums[i], running + nums[i])`, choosing the left option means…
options: Abandoning the previous run and starting a new subarray at i — done exactly when the old running sum went negative
explanation: `nums[i]` alone beats `running + nums[i]` precisely when running < 0 — a negative prefix is dead weight.

title: Drill: best time to sell (one pass)
prompt: From memory — the running-best shape on prices: track the MINIMUM price seen so far; at each day, profit if selling today = price - minSoFar; return the best such profit (0 if prices only fall).

solution.explanation: The best buy for a sale today is the minimum price seen before today, so one running minimum plus one running best covers every pair. (This is Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock, the same running-best shape as Kadane.) O(n) time, O(1) space.

hints: You only ever sell AFTER you buy. For today's sale, which earlier day is the best buy?
The cheapest price seen so far. Keep it as a running minimum while you scan.
Each day: `best = Math.max(best, p - minSoFar)`, then `minSoFar = Math.min(minSoFar, p)`.

title: Drill: can you reach the end? (jump)
prompt: From memory (reachability scan): `nums[i]` is the max jump from index i. Starting at 0, return whether the last index is reachable. Track the farthest reachable frontier.

solution.explanation: Every index up to `reach` can be reached, so the only thing that matters is the frontier. If the scan index ever passes it, there is an unreachable gap. O(n) time, O(1) space.

hints: Do the exact jumps matter, or only how far you could possibly get?
Keep `reach`, the farthest index reachable from any index you have been able to stand on.
If `i > reach`, you are stuck. Otherwise `reach = Math.max(reach, i + nums[i])`.

title: Why the gas-station reset is safe
prompt: In Gas Station you start at station 2, and the tank first goes negative when you arrive at station 5. Why is it safe to try station 6 next, skipping 3, 4 and 5?
options: Stations 3–5 were reached with a tank ≥ 0 from station 2. Starting at one of them means starting with 0 fuel, which is no better, so they also run dry by station 5
Each station can only be tried once
It isn't safe. It's a heuristic that happens to pass the tests
explanation: When you pass through any in-between station k from start 2, you arrive with fuel ≥ 0. Starting fresh at k gives you exactly 0 there, which can't do better, so k also fails by station 5. That exchange-style argument is what lets one O(n) pass replace trying all n starts.

title: Recall: Jump Game II levels
prompt: Fill in the BFS-by-levels template for the minimum number of jumps.
explanation: Stop before the last index, since standing on it needs no more jumps. `farthest` gathers the best reach of the current level. When `i` reaches `curEnd`, the level is used up: count a jump and make `farthest` the end of the next level.

title: Recall: Kadane + gas-station reset
prompt: Fill in the two running-sum templates: Kadane's maximum subarray, and the Gas Station restart.
explanation: Seed `best` with `nums[0]`, not 0, or all-negative arrays break. `max(nums[i], running + nums[i])` drops a negative prefix. In Gas Station, a negative tank at i rules out every start up to i, so the next candidate is `i + 1`.
